newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP year steel profit falls to A$133 mln.
newsitem.headline: BHP year steel profit falls to A$133 mln.

text.p: Australia's largest listed company and major steel producer, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, said on Friday that the 1996/97 (June-May) net profit including abnormal items from its steel division fell to A$133 million from A$155 million a year ago.
The company said it wrote down A$220 million from the steel division for the year ended May 31.
Excluding abnormal items, the annual net profit was 6.4 percent lower at A$353 million.

Sales revenue from the steel division rose by 8.7 percent to A$8.163 billion, mainly due to the inclusion of Tubemakers sales for the full year. This was partly offset by lower export steel revennue notwithstanding higher despatches from both Australia and New Zealand operations.

BHP said the net profit before abnormals also benefitted from cost reduction programmes, particularly in the second half. It said a negative influence on the profit result was higher raw material and labour costs and a higher depreciation charge mainly due to a newly commissioned plant at Port Kembla south of Sydney, in New South Wales.
